To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HCV NS3/NS4A protease and NS5B polymerase can cleave the HCV polyprotein in vitro.
HCV NS-5B polymerase has the ability to de novo initiate RNA synthesis in vitro, and that the de novo initiation is optimal with GTP as the first nucleotide.
HCV NS-5B polymerase can initiate RNA synthesis in vitro, and the initiation activity is dependent upon the template and nucleotide substrates used, as well as the reaction conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the initiation of HCV RNA synthesis by NS5B, a process that has not been previously reported.
the initiation of RNA synthesis by HCV NS-5B polymerase.
the initiation of RNA synthesis by HCV RdRp, which is an important step for the HCV replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCV NS 5B is able to initiate RNA synthesis de novo.
de novo priming is a property of the HCV RdRp.
the HCV RNA-dependent RNA polymerases can perform both de novo initiation of viral RNA synthesis and RNA synthesis by using the negative-strand RNA as the template.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HCV NS5 B protein is capable of de novo initiation of HCV RNA synthesis.
the HCV RNA-dependent RNA polymerization is capable of de novo initiation of nucleotide addition.
HCV NS3/4A protease, NS5B RdRp and RNA helicase, and NS3 helicase can be expressed in a single baculovirus expression vector and the recombinant proteins are active in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HCV NS4B protein has the capacity to initiate RNA synthesis de novo, which is a key step for the viral RNA replication.
HCV NS 5B has the capability of initiating RNA synthesis from a random nucleotide in the absence of a template.
HCV NS-5B is a bona fide RdRp that can initiate RNA synthesis de novo.
